title: Refit a window insect screen on its spring latches
instruction: Refit the insect screen in the window, seated on all four sides and latched, then let go of it.
context: Households take insect screens out to wash them and fit them back each season. This screen is held by two spring latches: each bolt sticks out past the screen's side, so the screen only passes between the jambs while both latch tabs are squeezed in, and it is held only when both bolts spring into their holes in the jambs with the screen square in the opening.
setup: Positions in metres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Window section (white-painted wood; jambs and head cropped to 40 mm wide), fixed: the wall below the window is a block x 0.284 to 0.440, |y| up to 0.37, 70 mm tall; its top is the stool (inside sill board) from x 0.284 and the opening's sill. Opening: jambs' inner faces at |y| = 0.206 (each 40 mm wide), their room-side faces at x = 0.344; head's underside 366 mm above the sill (10 mm above the seated screen); a wood-tone stop at x 0.400 to 0.412 behind the opening laps the screen's edge by 10 mm on all four sides (sill, head, both jambs); head 35 mm thick; 6 mm glass at x 0.424 to 0.430. Each jamb has a latch hole 10 mm (x) by 8 mm (height), 12 mm deep, centred at x = 0.3945 and 45 mm above the sill. Screen: 406 x 356 mm (16 x 14 in), 0.22 kg, mill aluminium frame 11.1 x 19.1 mm (7/16 x 3/4 in profile), charcoal fibreglass mesh. Near each bottom corner, on the room-side face, a black nylon latch housing (45 x 65 mm) carries a fixed lug and a tab (each 30 mm proud, 6 mm thick, 28 mm tall, centred 45 mm above the screen's bottom edge; lug centres 167 mm and tab centres 184 mm either side of the middle). Each tab drives a steel bolt (5.6 mm, 7/32 in) along the bottom of the side rail: at rest it stands 9.5 mm proud of the screen's side; squeezing the tab 11.5 mm toward the lug draws it 2 mm inside. Spring 250 N/m (about 1 N at rest, 3.9 N squeezed). Start, lot A: the screen stands on the table, centred on y = 0, leaning back 10 degrees with its back face against the stool's front edge, mesh and tabs toward the robot. Lot B moves it 25 mm to the robot's left, lot C 25 mm to the right. Trials are run on lots A, B and C and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. The arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Per trial, 0 if at any step the hands or the screen could not be read, or the screen was dropped (its origin falling faster than 0.5 m/s while every hand point is at least 20 mm from it). Seated on all four sides: every corner of its back face within 2 mm of the stop's face, both bottom corners from 1 mm below to 1.5 mm above the sill, within 2 degrees of upright and no side edge more than 0.5 mm past a jamb's face. A bolt is latched when its end is inside its jamb hole and at least 3 mm past the jamb's face. 1.0 seated with both bolts latched; 0.5 seated with one latched; 0 otherwise. Credit needs every sampled point of both grippers and fingertips (hull faces every 3 mm) more than 5 mm from the screen and its latches, and the screen and latches still (no point moving more than 1 mm) for 1 s. Doing nothing scores 0. Trials are run on each of lots A, B and C and averaged.
run_limit: 700 steps (35 seconds at 20 Hz) per lot
reset_notes: 1. Squeeze both latch tabs toward their lugs, pull the screen's bottom out of the opening and lift it out. 2. Release the tabs. 3. Stand the screen on the table in front of the stool, mesh and tabs toward the robot, its bottom edge parallel to the stool, and lean it back until its back face rests on the stool's front edge (about 10 degrees). 4. Centre it on y = 0 (lot A), 25 mm to the robot's left (lot B) or 25 mm to its right (lot C). 5. Return both arms to the ready pose.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Each latch is one sliding link (tab and bolt) on a 250 N/m spring with 4 mm preload against its stop; the rate is an estimate. Screen frame and mesh are one rigid body (mesh flex plays no part). Window cropped beyond the jambs, wall above and beside omitted. Hole size, play (3 mm a side) and tab size are chosen, not measured on one product. Friction 0.6. Lots stop a fixed replay, not one memorised per lot.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A, B, C); demo: 1.0 in each lot
